To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the motivational beliefs of East Asia students have the strongest association with science achievement, followed by Western Europe, North America and the other countries, while students in Latin America, Middle East and North Africa have the weakest associations.
self-concept has the strongest relationship to science achievement, followed by intrinsic value, utility value, and expectancy.
the three motivational beliefs have different predictive power for science achievement within an International context and the pattern is not identical across countries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relations between motivational beliefs in science and science achievement in an international context.
the cross-cultural differences in the associations between the three motivational constructs and science achievement.
the motivational beliefs of adolescents from a cross cultural perspective.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the motivational beliefs are important to student learning, and the patterns of motivational beliefs in relation to student achievement vary from country to country.
the relations among motivational beliefs in science and science achievement are different across countries, but they are not random.
self concept and intrinsic value are two important predictors of student achievement in most of the countries, but the predictive magnitude of utility value varies across countries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
motivational beliefs in science are not the same in every country, which may be related to the differences in the educational and cultural contexts.
motivational beliefs are important for science achievement in general.
the expectancy and task values have differential predictive power for explaining student achievement in science.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the international pattern of motivational beliefs in science achievement should be interpreted with caution in the cross-cultural perspective, as there are some countries whose patterns do not fit the international trend.
the predictive magnitudes for the three motivational beliefs in science achievement vary from country to country, and that the patterns are not identical.
motivational beliefs are important predictors of student achievement.
